findings.location: ExactResolutionDecisionV2 and ExactCrossRepositoryEdgeEvidence sections, lines 38-80; exact-resolution-and-flow-planning.md Resolution transaction and Flow Group seed contract, lines 94-113
findings.affected_requirement: Spec FR-006, FR-008, FR-012, FR-018 and SC-002/SC-003; existing Document graph uniqueness contract
findings.evidence: The corrected plan still assigns every ExactMatch decision its own deterministic EdgeId and persists its endpoint/consumer-candidate decision in ExactCrossRepositoryEdgeEvidence, which remains a one-to-one PK/FK extension of DocumentEdge. The existing repository model enforces a unique DocumentEdge on (SourceDocumentVersionId, TargetDocumentVersionId, EdgeType). Therefore two distinct endpoints or consumer entries in the same consumer Code Logic Document Version that resolve to the same provider XML Code Logic Document Version cannot both persist: the second deterministic Edge conflicts with the unique graph edge, while sharing the first Edge cannot work because one ExactCrossRepositoryEdgeEvidence row can hold only one consumer candidate, endpoint, decision fingerprint and evidence set. Flow Groups are endpoint/consumer-entry-centered and seed only from current v2 exact Edge evidence, so this is not merely duplicate graph display; it makes a valid second resolution/group unrepresentable.
findings.correction_outcome: Separate the document-level REFERENCES Edge identity from endpoint/consumer-entry resolution-decision identity. Preserve one reusable graph Edge per unique source/target/type while persisting one durable versioned exact-match decision/evidence record per pair + consumer entry + protocol + normalized endpoint + provider identity, with many decisions allowed to reference one graph Edge. Define legacy one-to-one compatibility, exact replay and changed-replay rules, Uncertainty transition ownership, contribution ownership, Flow Group seeding from the exact decision rather than an ambiguous edge row, migration keys/FKs/checks, and vectors for two endpoints and two consumer entries sharing one consumer/provider Document pair as well as exact duplicate replay.

summary: REVISE. S12-4-PR-001 is closed: the corrected artifacts consistently separate pair-specific Flow Group identity from business-flow-logical-key/1.0, define the cross-version consumer entry locator, use the existing unique Logical Document stable-key index and current-pointer concurrency token, and specify cross-pair append/supersede tests. S12-4-PR-002 is closed: provider evidence occurrences are canonically aggregated by one current provider XML Document Version before provider cardinality, persisted as reconstructable contribution rows, and tested against two distinct providers. The full fresh review found one new High plan-owned repository-fit defect: endpoint/consumer-entry exact decisions remain one-to-one with a DocumentEdge whose existing unique source/target/type constraint permits only one graph Edge for the same Document pair. The plan must introduce a many-decisions-to-one-Edge persistence seam before tasks. The three planned-change triggers remain accurate and still require explicit user authorization only after a corrected independent plan-review ACCEPT and before task generation; no authorization should be requested against this revised boundary. The nonrecursive boundary identity is SHA-256 over sorted path-tab-file-SHA256 lines for the nine pinned raw definition artifacts.
